html:
SMTO-EXE-0168 — The document changed after SMTO read it

GUID: d02ecb18-ed83-59b0-aab7-7f79b62df5d0
Slug: office-document-stale
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • Someone or something changed this document after SMTO looked at it, so SMTO stopped instead of applying an edit to the wrong content. No new copy was saved and the original wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the document is open in Word, Excel or PowerPoint, or is being synced from a shared folder, save any changes and close it there. Edits made elsewhere while SMTO works change the file and stop SMTO's edit.
  2. Ask SMTO to read the document again, then repeat the change you wanted. SMTO needs a fresh look at the current version so its edit lands in the right place.
  3. Check SMTO's summary of the current document to make sure the change still makes sense. Someone else's edits may have already made or altered the change you asked for.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the new edited document without this message.

If it still fails

  • If it keeps happening, something may be changing the file constantly, such as a sync app. Copy the error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to force the old edit onto the new version.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Office operation stopped because the document no longer matches the revision SMTO read: expected_revision differed from the parsed snapshot, a File revision guard failed, or the source hash changed before output publication (office.document_stale).

What this means

  • The requested revision differed from the parsed source snapshot, a File revision guard failed or the source digest changed before output publication. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • The requested revision differed from the parsed source snapshot, a File revision guard failed or the source digest changed before output publication.

How to diagnose it

  • Reinspect the exact source on the same Gateway and compare revision/hash plus object references before deciding whether the edit still applies.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the exact file on the same Gateway to obtain the new revision and object refs, review the changed structure, and build the edit from those refs. Refs also expire when the Gateway restarts.
  • Read the exact file again on the same Gateway and use its new revision and object refs after reviewing the changed contents.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the exact file again on the same Gateway and use its new revision and object refs after reviewing the changed contents.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh reviewed source evidence matches through publication of a separate output.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
